title: The Book Fair Economy
description: Pinewood Elementary's PTA throws the most magical book fair in the county, run on Reading Points the kids earn and spend. Tonight a dad calls in because his second-grader came home eleven thousand points in the hole, his recess is garnished, and Treasurer Cheryl is issuing margin calls in glitter pen.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight it's pure childhood magic. Down at Pinewood Elementary, the PTA throws the most beloved book fair in the county. The kids earn little Reading Points, they spend them on books. It runs itself. Treasurer Cheryl, welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A book fair for second graders. Okay. That's wholesome. I have no notes.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: No notes, Barry, how sweet. Yes, every child opens a little account on day one. They read, the points accrue, and the points are theirs. <p:0.3> Mostly theirs.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You hear that, Barry? The points are theirs. Mostly. Now THAT'S community.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Yeah, hi, hello. My son Marcus came home from the book fair Thursday. <p:0.3> He owes the PTA eleven thousand Reading Points. He is SEVEN.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Eleven THOUSAND? How does a seven-year-old owe eleven thousand of anything?

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: He bought the deluxe pop-up shark book, dear, on margin. <p:0.3> A reader reaches, the balance reaches with him. That's not a debt. That's ambition.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: On MARGIN? You let a second grader buy a shark book on MARGIN, Cheryl?

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: And I'll note, dear, that tone during what is technically silent reading. <p:0.3> That's a little gift to the library. Two hundred points. In glitter pen.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She just charged him for the call. We're at eleven thousand two hundred.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Oh, hello, dear, it's Patricia, room-mom, table four. I just want to say my Hannah has been points-positive for THREE years. <p:0.3> A balance isn't a debt. It's a milestone.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: It is not a milestone, it's a margin call, lady. They garnished his RECESS.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now hold on, garnished recess, that's just a child learning to work off a position. That's stewardship, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Buddy sees the ledger. <p:0.3> Buddy has been WATCHING the boy's account.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who is that. Cheryl, who just said Buddy.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: That's Buddy the Bookworm, our mascot, dear. He handles enforcement now. <p:0.3> He volunteered.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Buddy did not volunteer. Buddy was PROMOTED. <p:0.3> Buddy holds the master ledger.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Why is the worm in a costume talking about my son in the third person?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Oh, don't fight Buddy, dear, it only adds to the balance. <p:0.3> When Hannah hit twenty thousand we threw a little party. It was a milestone.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Twenty thousand? Patricia, your daughter is in DEBT.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: And there's the word again, dear. Debt. <p:0.3> That's a little gift to the library. Five hundred points. In glitter pen.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Eleven thousand seven hundred. Ronnie, the number only goes UP.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Okay. Okay. I'll just pay it off myself. Cash. What's the door rate, Cheryl, give me the number.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: Oh, we don't take cash, dear. The points are now pegged to the parents' property. <p:0.3> So the boy's account is secured against your minivan.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Secured against his WHAT?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: You collateralized my van against a pop-up shark book? He is SEVEN, Cheryl!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: We lost the Honda, dear. <p:0.3> It was a milestone.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Buddy sees the van.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Recess!

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: Garnished.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: The van!

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: Pegged.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Milestone!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Buddy sees the LEDGER.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: He is SEVEN!

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: In glitter pen.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait. <p:0.3> Wait, hang on. Cheryl, you said the show. <p:0.3> You said our airtime opens an account.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: Mm. <p:0.3> The station's hour tonight has been converted to points, dear. At the door rate. <p:0.3> I've logged the host.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Logged the host. <p:0.3> Now Barry, that is the most magical book fair in the county. The kids read, the points accrue, the whole town learns to give back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, we're on the ledger. The station is on the ledger.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Buddy is in your parking lot. <p:0.3> Buddy has left Pinewood.

lines.speaker: treasurer-cheryl
lines.text: He's expanding, dear. The other schools are merging in. <p:0.3> Snazzie FM is just the first.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well there it is, folks. Pinewood Elementary, the most magical book fair in the county. We'll be right back, soon as we settle up.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He is seven, Ronnie. <p:0.3> The bookworm is in our parking lot. <p:0.3> And we owe nine hundred points for SAYING that.
